body: Forward test of the sector cycle/lead indicator method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.60 (naive base rate 0.45) that: BSE Ltd Q3 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations exceeds ₹1,566 cr (a new quarterly record). Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): H1 operational revenue ₹2,999 cr (+48%); transaction charges ₹2,456 cr (+60%). Index-options premium ADTV: Q1 FY27 ₹29,615 cr, Q2 ₹22,531 cr ('first sequential quarterly contraction'), then 'a decisive recovery in September and a record-breaking October 2026… highest ever monthly index options premium ADTV of Rs. 35,481' crore; record single-day expiry premium ₹85,356 cr on 22-Oct-2026. MSCI derivatives collaboration. Screener revenue (₹ cr): Q4 FY26 1,564, Q1 FY27 1,566, Q2 FY27 1,433; OPM 67–68%. Reasoning: Lead indicator: premium ADTV drives ~80% of revenue. A linear fit of Q1/Q2 (revenue ≈ ₹1,009 cr + 0.0188 × ADTV) says a Q3 average ADTV above ~₹29.7k cr beats the record; October alone ran at ₹35.5k. Risk: November–December fade or a SEBI F&O tightening. Above base. Resolution: YES if BSE's consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (results filing; screener.in 'Sales') is > ₹1,566 cr. Source: BSE Ltd Q3 FY27 results (NSE) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table. Resolve by 2027-02-28; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A naive forecaster gives a fast-growing exchange setting a new quarterly revenue record after a down quarter roughly 45% (records are set in about half of quarters in an uptrend).
